presentation.label: MIDI GENERATOR
presentation.summary: Looping shift registers write the notes of the Octatrack's MIDI tracks.
presentation.overview: In the style of the Music Thing Modular Turing Machine: each MIDI track can run its own loop of bits, 2 to 16 steps long, which advances once per trig and lifts the trig 0 to 24 semitones above its own NOTE. TURING LOCK decides how often a bit flips as it comes round: 127 repeats the phrase, 64 is random. The first phrase after a boot comes from the moment PLAY is pressed.
highlights: A register per MIDI track, each with its own LOCK and LENGTH
LOCK 127 freezes the current phrase; 64 lets it wander
Settings saved with the project; a new project starts with every track OFF
A new first phrase each boot, seeded from when PLAY is pressed
Follows the track's own trigs, NOTE, chord notes, TRAN and note lengths
usage: In PROJECT > CONTROL > MIDI SEQUENCER, pick a track with TURING TRACK and set TURING MODE to ON.
Turn TURING LOCK towards 127 to keep a phrase, towards 64 to let it change; TURING LENGTH sets the loop.

controls.name: TURING TRACK
controls.doc: The MIDI track that MODE, LOCK and LENGTH below edit; not saved

controls.name: TURING MODE
controls.doc: OFF leaves the track stock; ON lets its register write the notes

controls.name: TURING LOCK
controls.doc: Chance that a bit keeps its value as it loops: 127 never flips (the phrase repeats), 64 flips about half the time, 0 always flips (a phrase twice LENGTH, second half inverted)

controls.name: TURING LENGTH
controls.doc: Loop length in trigs, 2 to 16 (stored as length minus two)

limitations: Chromatic notes 0..24 semitones above each trig's NOTE; scale stages come later.
Settings are saved per project as #TURING_T<n> lines that stock loaders skip, not per Part. The registers are runtime state; a STOP and PLAY or a reload keeps them.
The boot seed is read from DMA timer 3 at the first Turing trig; the timer's behaviour on hardware is inferred from stock's own programming of it, not measured.
Not tested: arpeggiator, NOTE parameter locks, incoming MIDI notes, Part or pattern changes while playing, timing under load, hardware.

tests.summary: Emulator only: verify.py drives the panel under the ColdFire port, reads MIDI OUT and checks every note against a model of the engine with a fixed test seed, then boots twice without it. Cycles, memory totals and hardware are not measured.

access.location: PROJECT > CONTROL > MIDI SEQUENCER: TURING TRACK, MODE, LOCK and LENGTH, under CC DIRECT CONNECT.
steps: Press PROJ. Select CONTROL with UP/DOWN and press RIGHT.
Select MIDI SEQUENCER and press YES.
On TURING TRACK, press RIGHT or LEFT, or turn LEVEL, to pick the MIDI track to edit.
Set TURING MODE to ON, then TURING LOCK and TURING LENGTH; the page scrolls to show LENGTH.
